dataset.name: CUAD v1 — Contract Understanding Atticus Dataset
dataset.purpose: Question-answer annotations for finding contract-review clauses and their supporting text.

title.description: Contract identifier/title; use it as the document-level ID.

paragraphs.description: Text-and-annotation container. In this release, each contract has one long context entry.

context.example: This Agreement is made and entered into...
context.description: Full contract text in which labeled evidence is located.

qas.description: One review-category question and its evidence label(s), generally one record per category.

id.description: Unique annotation ID, combining a contract identifier and clause category.

question.example: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to \"Document Name\"...
question.description: Natural-language prompt naming the clause category and defining what to find.

is_impossible.description: false means the category has at least one labeled evidence span; true means no answer was annotated.

answers.description: Zero or more evidence spans. Empty when is_impossible is true; multiple spans may support the same category.

text.description: Exact contract text selected as evidence.

answer_start.description: Zero-based character offset where text begins inside its parent context string.

Category (incl. context and answer).description: The clause label used in the questions/annotation IDs.

Description.description: Plain-language definition of the clause category.

Answer Format.description: Expected form of the extracted answer, such as a date, entity name, or Yes/No.

Group.description: Optional category grouping code supplied by CUAD.

tree: file → data[] (contract) → paragraphs[] → { context, qas[] } → { id, question, is_impossible, answers[] } → { text, answer_start }

modeling_interpretation.input: context (or a chunk of it) plus a target clause category/question
modeling_interpretation.target: Whether the category appears and, when available, its answer-span evidence
modeling_interpretation.important_note: CUAD supplies clause evidence, not Low/Medium/High risk labels; risk labels must be created by a separate scoring rule or review process.
